title: Start here · regional vs global 40%
description: Natal homing, directional movement, and four SPR methods with one SPR-constrained yield benchmark.
focus: Compare Reg-Move with SpE-RecW: both meet a recruitment-weighted global SPR of 40%, but only Reg-Move explicitly targets 40% in each region. Here Yield-SPR overlaps Reg-Move; click the legend to inspect either curve. Pop-Move also coincides with Reg-Move under homing, so that duplicate is omitted.

title: Whose global 40%? · weighting choices
description: Metapopulation with destination biology: recruitment, equal, survey and catch weighting share a label but define different targets.
focus: Compare the regional SPRs from the four global weighting methods. The Global SPR · RecW column uses recruitment weights consistently for comparison; an equal-, survey- or catch-weighted method need not give 40% in that column.

title: Can both population targets be met?
description: Long-lived metapopulation with strong directional movement. Compare natal-population and regional SPR targets.
focus: Look for the Pop-Move availability message in the comparison table. This example illustrates a bounded search without an accepted population-target solution while the regional and global calculations remain usable; it is not a proof that every possible solution is absent.

title: SPR protection vs system MSY
description: Natal homing with Beverton–Holt recruitment: compare SPR rules, SPR-constrained yield and unconstrained system MSY.
focus: Compare Yield-SPR with Yield-Max · system MSY. Higher total yield can come with a regional SPR below 40%. SPR and biomass depletion are different quantities under Beverton–Holt; inspect both the SPR table and the biomass curves.

title: Seasonal movement + biomass feedback
description: Four different seasonal transfers in a metapopulation, with reduced historical biomass and annual fishing feedback.
focus: Open the movement editor to inspect the four transfers, then compare the F₁ and F₂ plots below catch. SPR rules adjust fishing with biomass; the Yield-SPR benchmark holds optimized F constant. Those projections therefore compare different implementation rules.

title: No movement · the control case
description: Two closed regions show which reference points coincide when movement is removed.
focus: SpE-RecW and SpD-RecW coincide; Reg-Move and Pop-NoMove coincide. Two regional targets can still require a different fishing ratio from the 70:30 global rule. Expected overlaps are useful checks, not missing curves.
